cases.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 47, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 11
Subject: Request for safety study at Cropsey Avenue & Bay Parkway

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

We write to ask for a safety study on your roads at Cropsey Avenue & Bay Parkway.

The official NYPD record for the 5 years from 2 November 2021 shows 113 crashes there, including 51 injury crashes that left 19 pedestrians injured and 3 cyclists injured. No deaths were recorded. This is a city priority location. Harm is about 3.5 million USD per year in the U.S. DOT's official values (2024 dollars).

The latest recorded treatment was turn traffic calming in 2021.

We request you consider, where suitable after site checks on your roads:

• a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green): expected to avoid about 0.4 pedestrian injury crashes per year, avoiding about 151,000 USD per year of that harm; it pays for itself in 1.1 million USD. Where the city installed it at 1,651 intersections, pedestrian injury crashes fell compared with intersections that got it later; a stricter check against fake programs is less certain.

• reflective backplates on the traffic signals: expected to avoid about 1.5 injury crashes per year, avoiding about 524,000 USD per year of that harm; it pays for itself in 3.7 million USD. What must be checked on site first is whether an entry on yellow or red is a factor.

This corner got turn traffic calming in 2021. Across the city a simple before/after comparison suggested a decline, but a check using a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program. Repeating it here is not supported by the city's own record. We ask for a different approach.

Please assess these fixes on the roads you own and advise on next steps.

Kind regards,

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
